article_title: A Game Design Methodology for Generating a Psychological Profile of Players
citation: Guardiola, E., & Natkin, S. (2015). A Game Design Methodology for Generating a Psychological Profile of Players. In Serious Games Analytics, Methodologies for Performance Measurement, Assessment, and Improvement. Springer. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-05834-4
title: JEU SERAI vocational guidance profiling game
description: JEU SERAI is a serious game whose ambition is "to help the vocational guidance of students and adults at an individual level", using game mechanisms to evaluate professional interest, motivation and decision taking. Built by a consortium of two companies, two universities and an adult training association, it contains 18 mini games, three for each Holland RIASEC type, distributed in an open world over three chapters, plus narrative questionnaires, recurrent activities and avatar clothing choices linked to RIASEC types. It produces a RIASEC profile for the player and a data file of item values for analysis.
requirements: Expert review pipeline for content validation
A documented interface linking in-game item values to RIASEC dimension scores
constraints: The goal is not to substitute for a career adviser but to offer an engaging way to make self-assessment psychometric tests
target_learners: middle school students to adults in career change
target_learning_goals: vocational interest self-assessment via RIASEC profile
examples: Mini games include Nice Apple (Realistic, apple harvesting), Omelet (Enterprising, directing a team) and Classified (Conventional, classifying stamps)
key_sources: Guardiola, E., & Natkin, S. (2015). A Game Design Methodology for Generating a Psychological Profile of Players. In Serious Games Analytics, Methodologies for Performance Measurement, Assessment, and Improvement. Springer. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-05834-4_16

article_title: Designing, Implementing and Evaluating Preclinical Simulation Lab for Maternity Nursing Course
citation: Haya ALFozan, Yousria El Sayed, Farida Habib. (2015). Designing, Implementing and Evaluating Preclinical Simulation Lab for Maternity Nursing Course. Journal of Education and Practice, Vol.6, No.12. https://www.iiste.org/journals/
title: Jeffries/National League for Nursing Framework for Designing, Implementing and Evaluating Simulations
description: The article situates its simulation course design in the Jeffries/National League for Nursing Framework for Designing, Implementing and Evaluating Simulations, which it links to Lindsey and Berger's "three universal principles for experiential instruction - framing, activating, and reflecting on the experience". The framework underlies the study's briefing-practice-debriefing structure and the Jeffries (2005) perception questionnaire used for evaluation, whose five categories are Objectives and Information, Student Support, Problem Solving, Feedback/Guided Reflection, and Fidelity (Realism).
requirements: Simulation-based courses following this structure consist of an initial briefing followed by participation in the experience and then a debriefing
target_learners: pre-licensure nursing students in simulation-based clinical courses
target_learning_goals: clinical skills, decision making, and clinical judgment in a safe simulated environment
examples: The study used Jeffries' (2005) 20-item perception questionnaire in five categories to evaluate the preclinical simulation sessions
key_sources: Haya ALFozan, Yousria El Sayed, Farida Habib. (2015). Designing, Implementing and Evaluating Preclinical Simulation Lab for Maternity Nursing Course. Journal of Education and Practice, Vol.6, No.12. https://www.iiste.org/journals/

article_title: Toward Social Justice: The Characteristics of an Effective Mathematics Intervention Program for Urban Middle School Students
citation: Bowens, B. D., & Warren, S. R. (2016). Toward Social Justice: The Characteristics of an Effective Mathematics Intervention Program for Urban Middle School Students. Journal of Urban Learning Teaching and Research, 12, 35-46. https://eric.ed.gov/?q=Toward+Social+Justice+Characteristics+of+an+Effective+Mathematics+Intervention+Program
title: The Jaime Escalante Math Program (JEMP): a six-week intensive summer mathematics intervention for urban middle school students
description: The JEMP is a foundation-sponsored summer mathematics intervention providing "secondary mathematics intervention and enrichment to students of color and low-income students in urban communities of greater Los Angeles" for over 35 years, in partnership with 128 area schools and East Los Angeles Community College. It is a "6-weeks intensive 145-hour summer program" serving predominantly low-income, minority students, with diagnostic pre/post assessments, daily homework, college tutors in every classroom, and classes of 25 or fewer. The study evaluated its achievement effects and identified its program characteristics.
requirements: Teachers hold a bachelor's degree in math and a teaching credential with 5 years experience, with 3-10 hours of professional development per teacher and individualized training based on classroom observations
constraints: The program works individually with schools to create programs addressing the unique needs of their students
target_learners: urban middle school students entering 7th and 8th grade who are behind in math, predominantly low-income and minority
target_learning_goals: pre-algebra and algebra readiness and achievement
matriculation into college and math-related careers
examples: Students entering 7th and 8th grade took MDTP diagnostic readiness tests at the beginning and end of the six-week summer program at one district-designated school
key_sources: Bowens, B. D., & Warren, S. R. (2016). Toward Social Justice: The Characteristics of an Effective Mathematics Intervention Program for Urban Middle School Students. Journal of Urban Learning Teaching and Research, 12, 35-46. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1119158

article_title: Gamify Online Courses with Tools Built into Your Learning Management System (LMS) to Enhance Self-Determined and Active Learning
citation: Chen, C.-C., Huang, C., Gribbins, M., & Swan, K. (2018). Gamify online courses with tools built into your learning management system (LMS) to enhance self-determined and active learning. Online Learning, 22(3), 41-54. https://doi.org/10.24059/olj.v22i3.1466
title: Jeopardy Exam Review: a wiki-based LMS review game with difficulty-ranked categories and dollar-value rewards
description: A six-category online Jeopardy game built in an LMS wiki with a 6 x 5 table. "The 'dollar' value earned with each correct answer increased as the question's difficulty increased." Rows were ranked from easiest to most difficult with more difficult answers worth more points. Instructional videos explaining each question's solution were provided after the game ended.
requirements: An LMS with built-in wiki functionality allowing editable tables and single-user editing locks
constraints: Storytelling, theme, role-playing, and replayability elements were not implemented (marked N/A in Table 2)
target_learners: Graduate students in online statistics courses
target_learning_goals: Review key statistical concepts for exam preparation
examples: Played for an entire week during the 16-week semester
key_sources: Chen, C.-C., Huang, C., Gribbins, M., & Swan, K. (2018). Gamify online courses with tools built into your learning management system (LMS) to enhance self-determined and active learning. Online Learning, 22(3), 41-54. https://doi.org/10.24059/olj.v22i3.1466

article_title: Effect of the Jeffries Simulation Framework on the Core Competence of New Graduate Paediatric Surgery Nurses: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
citation: Luo Wenjing, Yang Runyu, Feng Liwei, and Liang Yuanyuan. 2026. "Effect of the Jeffries Simulation Framework on the Core Competence of New Graduate Paediatric Surgery Nurses: A Quasi‐Experimental Study." Nursing Open 13 (9): e70779. https://doi.org/10.1002/nop2.70779
title: Jeffries simulation framework as a design structure for simulation-based nursing instruction
description: The Jeffries simulation framework is an experiential-learning-based framework for designing simulation-based instruction in nursing education. The article describes it as consisting of "context, background, design, educational practices, simulation experience and outcomes", and notes it is "based on experiential learning theory and is specifically designed for simulation‐based instruction". In this study, the framework structured the design of clinical scenario simulation cases used to train new graduate paediatric surgery nurses over 8 weeks.
requirements: Simulation courses designed with the framework require trained teachers, preset clinical scenarios with role assignment, and teacher-guided debriefing sessions
constraints: The article notes the framework version used "does not utilize simulated patients (SPs)", focusing instead on role play based on authentic clinical cases
examples: Clinical scenarios covered paediatric intestinal, orthopaedic, hepatobiliary, and acute and critical diseases; sessions ran 35–70 min with RUST-structured debriefing
key_sources: Luo Wenjing, Yang Runyu, Feng Liwei, and Liang Yuanyuan. 2026. "Effect of the Jeffries Simulation Framework on the Core Competence of New Graduate Paediatric Surgery Nurses: A Quasi‐Experimental Study." Nursing Open 13 (9): e70779. https://doi.org/10.1002/nop2.70779

article_title: Evaluating the impact of a BOPPPS and scenario-based simulation intervention on the competency of junior circulating nurses: a quasi-experimental study.
citation: Li Mu, Cheng Wang. (2026). Evaluating the impact of a BOPPPS and scenario-based simulation intervention on the competency of junior circulating nurses: a quasi-experimental study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-08712-y
title: Jeffries Simulation Theory as the theoretical bridge aligning BOPPPS phases with simulation design
description: The study employs Jeffries Simulation Theory, whose core elements the article names as "Background, Design, Simulation Experience, Assessment, and Debriefing", systematically aligned with the six BOPPPS modules to form a closed loop of objective–simulation–reflection. Bridge-in and Objectives map to Background and Design; Pre-assessment refines Design by gauging baseline skills; Participatory Learning embodies the Simulation Experience; Post-assessment and Summary align with Assessment and Debriefing through structured evaluation and facilitated debriefing. The article describes the framework as grounded in experiential learning theory and widely adopted to guide simulation-based instructional design.
requirements: Requires alignment of each BOPPPS phase with a Jeffries element, including structured evaluation tools and facilitated debriefing in the Post-assessment and Summary phases
constraints: The article notes debriefing sessions that fail to provoke deep reflection, or inaccurate pre-assessment, can leave learning at the level of superficial practice
target_learners: Junior circulating nurses (N2 level, 3–5 years experience)
target_learning_goals: Circulating-nurse competencies: clinical decision-making, priority management, teamwork, emergency response
examples: The training mapped Bridge-in and Pre-assessment onto a five-day video observation period that simultaneously identified problems and established baselines
key_sources: Li Mu, Cheng Wang. (2026). Evaluating the impact of a BOPPPS and scenario-based simulation intervention on the competency of junior circulating nurses: a quasi-experimental study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-08712-y

article_title: Simulated communication and teamwork scenario for nursing students: construction and validity.
citation: Silva Aline Teixeira; Leal Laura Andrian; Ribeiro Maria Inês Lemos Coelho; Hilário Jeniffer Stephanie Marques; da Silva Monise Martins; Alves Mateus Goulart; Januário Gabriela da Cunha; Henriques Sílvia Helena. (2025). Simulated communication and teamwork scenario for nursing students: construction and validity. Revista Brasileira de Enfermagem. https://doi.org/10.1590/0034-7167-2024-0600
title: Jeffries design model as the methodological framework for scenario construction
description: The study adopted the Jeffries design model as its methodological framework for building the simulated scenario, alongside the International Nursing Association for Clinical Simulation and Learning guidelines. The article states the model "works on student support, simulation objectives, problem-solving, fidelity and debriefing", and the INACSL guidelines structured the scenario around "the briefing, scenario in action and debriefing phases" with a basis in interprofessional education. These frameworks shaped the scenario's topics, timing and checklist domains.
requirements: Attention to student support, simulation objectives, problem-solving, fidelity and debriefing when designing a simulation
target_learners: undergraduate nursing students in simulation-based education
examples: The scenario chart enumerates target audience, objectives, estimated time, briefing, development, assessment, expected actions, evolution, debriefing, environment, participants, and materials.
key_sources: Silva Aline Teixeira; Leal Laura Andrian; Ribeiro Maria Inês Lemos Coelho; Hilário Jeniffer Stephanie Marques; da Silva Monise Martins; Alves Mateus Goulart; Januário Gabriela da Cunha; Henriques Sílvia Helena. (2025). Simulated communication and teamwork scenario for nursing students: construction and validity. Revista Brasileira de Enfermagem. https://doi.org/10.1590/0034-7167-2024-0600

article_title: Clinical simulation for nurses' knowledge on postpartum hemorrhage: a randomized clinical trial.
citation: Coelho Tatiane da Silva, Fonseca Luciana Mara Monti, Cardoso Maria Vera Lúcia Moreira Leitão, Aquino Priscila de Souza, da Costa Camila Chaves, Maciel Nathanael de Souza, Damasceno Ana Kelve de Castro. (2025). Clinical simulation for nurses' knowledge on postpartum hemorrhage: a randomized clinical trial. Revista Brasileira de Enfermagem. https://doi.org/10.1590/0034-7167-2024-0214
title: Jeffries simulation framework for designing, implementing and evaluating simulations as teaching strategies in nursing
description: The study was based on the simulation model proposed by Pamela Jeffries, which "provides a framework for designing, implementing, and evaluating simulations used as teaching strategies in nursing" and specifies relevant variables and their relationships to support research identifying effective and ineffective practices. Its key elements span eight areas: simulation design, outcomes and objectives, facilitation, debriefing, participant evaluation, professional integrity, interprofessional education enhanced by simulation, and a simulation glossary. The article used it, with INACSL guidelines, to guide the scenario's design and the teaching-learning process.
requirements: The article states a consistent, empirically supported model is needed to guide the design and implementation of simulations and evaluate outcomes
constraints: The framework is described for nursing simulation contexts
target_learners: Nurses and nursing students in clinical education
target_learning_goals: Clinical competencies, decision-making, and knowledge acquisition through simulation-based experiences
examples: The PPH scenario in this trial was developed following the framework's recommendations, including structured debriefing and participant evaluation via a checklist
key_sources: Coelho Tatiane da Silva, Fonseca Luciana Mara Monti, Cardoso Maria Vera Lúcia Moreira Leitão, Aquino Priscila de Souza, da Costa Camila Chaves, Maciel Nathanael de Souza, Damasceno Ana Kelve de Castro. (2025). Clinical simulation for nurses' knowledge on postpartum hemorrhage: a randomized clinical trial. Revista Brasileira de Enfermagem. https://doi.org/10.1590/0034-7167-2024-0214

article_title: Interdisciplinary simulation scenario in nursing education: Humanized childbirth and birth.
citation: Fonseca LMM, Monteiro JCS, Aredes ND, Bueno JV, Domingues AN, Coutinho VRD, Baptista RCN. (2020). Interdisciplinary simulation scenario in nursing education: Humanized childbirth and birth. Revista Latino-Americana de Enfermagem. https://doi.org/10.1590/1518-8345.3681.3286
title: Jeffries framework with INACSL standards as the structure for developing simulation scenarios
description: The article operationalizes the Jeffries framework, "which consists of the following elements: Theme identification, simulation objectives, participants, scenario and debriefing process", combined with elaboration guides standardized by the International Nursing Association for Clinical Simulation in Learning. The scenario's components — objectives, resources, prebriefing, scene description, roles and checklist — follow this structure, and the authors state that knowledge of "methods, models and standardized simulation guides by teachers are fundamental aspects for its implementation in the curriculum".
requirements: Teachers and facilitators need knowledge of simulation methods, models and standardized guides such as Jeffries and INACSL to implement scenarios in the curriculum
examples: The scenario was developed as an activity of a teacher training course given by European simulation specialists and improved with participant and specialist suggestions
key_sources: Fonseca LMM, Monteiro JCS, Aredes ND, Bueno JV, Domingues AN, Coutinho VRD, Baptista RCN. (2020). Interdisciplinary simulation scenario in nursing education: Humanized childbirth and birth. Revista Latino-Americana de Enfermagem. https://doi.org/10.1590/1518-8345.3681.3286
